pages.title: Generic Programming
pages.content:
Generics let a class or method work with a family of reference types while preserving compile-time type safety.

For example, `Box<String>` stores strings, while `Box<Integer>` stores integers. The compiler checks that the declared type is used consistently.

callout.title: Key Concept
callout.text: Generic Programming explains a Java design rule used in Generic programming: classes, methods.

codeCard.code: class Box<T>{T value;Box(T v){value=v;}T get(){return value;}} public class Main { public static void main(String[] a){Box<String> b=new Box<>("Java");System.out.println(b.get());}}

checkpoint.question: What should you verify when applying Generic Programming in Java?
options: The declaration, visibility, and runtime behavior must match the rules of Generic Programming.
Every class must inherit from two concrete classes.
checkpoint.explanation: The correct choice applies the Java/OOP rule associated with Generic Programming without introducing unrelated state or unsafe behavior.

pages.title: Generic Methods
pages.content:
A generic method declares its type parameter before the return type, such as `<T> T first(T a, T b)`.

Type inference often lets the caller omit the type argument, while the compiler still checks the operations permitted for the type parameter.

callout.title: Key Concept
callout.text: Generic Methods explains a Java design rule used in Generic programming: classes, methods.

codeCard.code: public class Main { static <T> void show(T x){System.out.println(x);} public static void main(String[] a){show("Java");}}

pages.title: How to use Generic Methods
pages.content:
Generic methods are useful when the same operation should work for many types without duplicated implementations.

When the method needs specific capabilities, a bounded type parameter such as `<T extends Number>` can constrain the accepted types while retaining genericity.

callout.title: Key Concept
callout.text: How to use Generic Methods explains a Java design rule used in Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: Step-by-step learning path
pages.content: Follow this exact sequence for **Generic programming: classes, methods**: prerequisite check → concept build → mental model → worked example → dry run → guided implementation → independent practice → mastery gate. Do not skip to the final practice set until the guided implementation is understood.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete step-by-step learning path for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 1. Prerequisite check
pages.content: Before starting **Generic programming: classes, methods**, recall the Java syntax and object/model concepts required for it. Write down what you already know, then identify one question you cannot yet answer confidently. The purpose of this step is to expose a missing prerequisite before new material is introduced.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 1. prerequisite check for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 2. Build the concept
pages.content: Generics move type errors from runtime to compile time and reduce casting. A generic type parameter describes a family of related types without giving up type safety. Start with the rule, then connect the rule to one small Java example. Avoid memorizing a code template before you can explain why each important line is present.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 2. build the concept for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 3. Build a mental model
pages.content: Imagine the runtime state while **Generic programming: classes, methods** executes. Identify the important actors, ownership, values, references, control flow, or exception paths. Explain the relationship in plain language before touching a full program.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 3. build a mental model for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 4. Worked example
pages.content: Take one small example for **Generic programming: classes, methods** and solve it in visible steps: state the input, apply the first rule, update the state, and predict the output or effect. Then compare your reasoning with the executable example in this topic.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 4. worked example for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 5. Dry run before execution
pages.content: Trace the program line by line using a state table. Record changed variables, object fields, references, collections, thread state, or exception flow. The goal is to make the execution predictable rather than mysterious.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 5. dry run before execution for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 6. Guided implementation
pages.content: Implement a minimal version of **Generic programming: classes, methods** using the starter structure supplied in the practice problem. First fill in the missing concept, then run the smallest sample, then expand to a second case. Do not optimize before the behavior is correct.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 6. guided implementation for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 7. Independent practice
pages.content: Solve the **Generic programming: classes, methods** practice problems in increasing difficulty. For every failure, classify it as syntax, concept, state-tracing, edge-case, or design error before changing the code.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 7. independent practice for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 8. Mastery gate
pages.content: You have mastered **Generic programming: classes, methods** when you can: (1) explain the rule without notes, (2) dry-run a new example, (3) implement a small variation, (4) explain one common failure, and (5) choose when the concept should and should not be used.
pages.teachingGoal: Learner can complete 8. mastery gate for Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 9. Debugging and misconception clinic
pages.content:
Use the following diagnostic routine:

- **Mistake:** Memorizing Generic programming: classes, methods syntax without understanding its runtime behavior. 
  **Recovery:** return to the smallest example, state the governing rule, and rerun one change at a time.
- **Mistake:** Skipping prerequisite concepts and guessing from compiler errors alone. 
  **Recovery:** return to the smallest example, state the governing rule, and rerun one change at a time.
- **Mistake:** Testing only the sample input. 
  **Recovery:** return to the smallest example, state the governing rule, and rerun one change at a time.
- **Mistake:** Changing several parts of the program before identifying the failing concept. 
  **Recovery:** return to the smallest example, state the governing rule, and rerun one change at a time.
pages.teachingGoal: Diagnose common errors while learning Generic programming: classes, methods.

pages.title: 10. Mastery review and interview transfer
pages.content:
Finish **Generic programming: classes, methods** by answering these without notes:

1. What problem does this concept solve?
2. What is the smallest correct example?
3. What invariant or rule must remain true?
4. What edge case commonly breaks naive solutions?
5. What is one interview question you could answer from this topic?

Then solve one unseen variation before marking the topic complete.

pages.title: Concept and mental model
pages.content:
### Generic Classes and Methods

Generic Classes and Methods becomes useful when Java code needs to express a stable rule rather than a one-off syntax trick. Start with the mental model: identify the values or states involved, the operation Java performs, and the contract the surrounding code expects.

**Learning focus**
- **type parameter** — understand the rule and when it belongs in a production design.
- **generic class** — understand the rule and when it belongs in a production design.
- **generic method** — understand the rule and when it belongs in a production design.
- **diamond operator** — understand the rule and when it belongs in a production design.
- **type inference** — understand the rule and when it belongs in a production design.

**Rule before API:** before choosing a class or method, state what must be true before the operation, what it produces, and what can fail. This keeps advanced Java from becoming API memorization.
pages.teachingGoal: Explain the mental model behind Generic Classes and Methods and state when the feature should be used.

pages.title: API anatomy and design rules
pages.content:
### API anatomy

A production learner should know not just *what* an API call does, but what contract surrounds it. For **Generic Classes and Methods**, pay attention to:

1. **Inputs and types:** what values are accepted?
2. **State:** what data is owned or shared?
3. **Failure modes:** which errors are compile-time, runtime, or domain failures?
4. **Lifetime:** what must be closed, awaited, copied, or released?
5. **Observability:** how can you prove the operation produced the correct result?

**Design rule:** prefer the narrowest abstraction that expresses the contract. Expose stable interfaces and value objects at boundaries; keep mutable implementation details private.

pages.title: Debugging and failure analysis
pages.content:
### Debugging Generic Classes and Methods

When a program fails, classify the failure before changing code:

**Compile-time:** the type or API contract is invalid.

**Runtime:** the program reaches an operation whose preconditions are violated.

**Logic:** the program runs but produces an incorrect state or output.

**Concurrency / lifecycle:** the code is valid in isolation but fails because timing, ownership, cleanup, or shared state was handled incorrectly.

- **Using raw types:** apply the rule, isolate the smallest failing case, and verify the corrected behavior.
- **Adding casts to hide a weak generic design:** apply the rule, isolate the smallest failing case, and verify the corrected behavior.
- **Using Object where a type parameter is sufficient:** apply the rule, isolate the smallest failing case, and verify the corrected behavior.
- **Assuming generics work with primitives:** apply the rule, isolate the smallest failing case, and verify the corrected behavior.

**Debugging loop:** reproduce -> isolate -> state the rule -> fix one cause -> rerun the smallest failing case.

pages.title: Mastery and interview review
pages.content:
### Mastery review

Before moving on, you should be able to explain **Generic Classes and Methods** without looking at code, implement the smallest correct version, identify one edge case, and justify one API-design choice.

**Mastery checklist**
- [ ] Create reusable classes with type parameters.
- [ ] Write generic methods without unsafe casts.
- [ ] Choose type parameters that reflect the API contract.

**Interview connection:** explain the feature in 30 seconds, give one runnable example, and name one failure mode or design trade-off.

**Transfer challenge:** change one requirement in the examples and predict what part of the implementation must change.
